extracted.intended_audience: policymakers, government e-participation designers, and researchers in rulemaking/e-government
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing, deploying, and evaluating online participation platforms (e.g., RegulationRoom.org) to achieve broader and higher-quality public engagement in complex government rulemaking. Emphasizes technical design plus procedural, social, and psychological supports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacities required for effective civic engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The platform must identify, nurture, and support the capacities that citizens need to engage meaningfully with complex policymaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: RegulationRoom.org is used as a case study to address what capacities are required for effective civic engagement and how they can be nurtured and supported by an online participation system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technology design is necessary but insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Effectively designing and deploying technology, although essential, is only one dimension of realizing broader, better online civic engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers should not assume technology alone will produce meaningful participation; other dimensions (procedural, social, psychological) must be addressed alongside technical design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address procedural, social, and psychological barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective e-participation systems must be prepared to address procedural, social, and psychological barriers that impede citizens’ meaningful participation in complex policymaking processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Platforms should include features, processes, and supports that reduce or mitigate procedural complexity, social exclusion or dynamics, and psychological obstacles (e.g., intimidation, lack of confidence, perceived futility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-conceptualize the value of broad civic participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymakers and designers need to re-conceptualize the value that broad civic participation brings to policymaking processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes recognizing different forms of value (not only expert technical input) that broader participation can provide and adjusting expectations and decision processes accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize novice commenters engage differently than experienced insiders
rubrics_metrics.description: Novice commenters engage with policy issues differently than experienced insiders, and systems should be designed with those differences in mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers should tailor interfaces, guidance, and interaction protocols to support novices (e.g., scaffolding, plain-language explanations, guided prompts) rather than assuming expert behaviors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize and accept non-traditional forms of knowledge and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Government decision makers and participation designers must be open to recognizing non-traditional forms of knowledge and styles of communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be willing to devise participation mechanisms and protocols that can capture, interpret, and use diverse knowledge forms and communication styles rather than privileging traditional technical comment formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Devise participation mechanisms and protocols accordingly
rubrics_metrics.description: Participation mechanisms and protocols should be devised to accommodate varied contributors and communication forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanisms may include alternate submission formats, summaries, translation between lay and technical framing, moderation/curation strategies, and explicit rules for how different inputs are used in decisionmaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit resources to achieve broader and better participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting better participation from more people requires the investment of resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policymakers and platform operators should be prepared to allocate funding, staff time, outreach, facilitation, and other resources necessary to recruit, support, and integrate broader participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make statutory transparency and participation rights meaningful by reducing barriers
rubrics_metrics.description: Although broad transparency and participation rights are part of the legal structure, significant barriers prevent effective engagement by many citizens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should focus on translating legal rights into practicable opportunities through lowering entry costs, clarifying procedures, providing supports, and ensuring access to information and deliberative tools.
